requirement:
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
path.
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.index.detail_pages`. I did not request implementation source.

- **One page per requirement and named example.**
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` renders two requirements (`zeta`, `cli.mdbook`), one example (`alpha`) and a requirement in a nested child chapter (`nested`).
  - It asserts that the index holds exactly those four detail pages plus "Coverage gaps".
  - The definition chapters keep no detail sub-items of their own, apart from the existing "Child" chapter.
  - `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` covers requirements in every evidence state, including `absent` (Missing), which gets a page whose `source_path` points back at the definition chapter.
  - `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` covers a FIXME-state requirement.
  - `tests/repository.rs#fn[mdbook_preprocessor_renders_definitions_between_stdin_and_stdout]` covers the real `habeas mdbook` binary.
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers the case with no definitions, where the index has only "Coverage gaps".
- **Subchapter of the index chapter.** Detail pages are checked as `sub_items` of the index with `parent_names == ["Requirements index"]` or `["Index"]`. This holds for both the default index and an explicit index placed elsewhere, in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]`.
- **Definition order.**
  - The name list `rules.zeta`, `rules.alpha`, `rules.cli.mdbook`, `rules.child.nested` is asserted in order. That order mixes a requirement and an example and puts the nested chapter last.
  - Section numbers `[3, offset+2]` are asserted in the same test, and `[3,4]` in the explicit-index test.
  - Across chapters, the explicit-index test asserts the order `rules.zeta`, `more.cli.mdbook`.
- **Titled by the full name.** The `name` assertions use full names such as `rules.zeta` and `more.cli.mdbook`, and `requirements.core.ready` in the `src/index.rs` test.
- **Path derived from the index path.**
  - `src/index.rs` asserts the path `appendix/requirements-index/requirements.core.ready.md` for an index at `appendix/requirements-index.md`.
  - The default index at `requirements-index.md` gets "Coverage gaps" at `requirements-index/coverage.md`.
  - Links from definitions and the index into `requirements-index/...html` and `appendix/index/more.cli%2Emdbook.html` confirm the derivation for other index locations and for names containing dots.
  - I found no direct assertion of the `.md` path for a `cli.mdbook`-style name. The link href assertions cover that name's derived location, so I don't treat it as a gap.
- **Folding via the cited `requirements.cli.setup`.**
  - `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_is_repeatable]` asserts that setup writes `output.html.fold.enable = true` exactly once, even when run twice.
  - `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_keeps_an_existing_fold_setting]` asserts that an existing `enable = false` is kept, and that `enable = true` is added when only `level` is set.
  - Together these cover applying the cited setup requirement in this subject's case.

I found no unaddressed obligation or missing scenario.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
